output.summary: A strongly scented herb native across much of Eurasia, Macaronesia and North Africa, celery grows naturally in damp, often salty places. Cultivated forms are vegetables selected for edible leaf stalks, swollen stem bases, or leaves and stems, which may be eaten raw or cooked.
output.edibilityNote: Wild celery was historically a condiment; cultivated forms provide raw or cooked stalks, swollen stem bases, leaves and stems.
